risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- MD&A 'Risk and Concerns' names climate change as one of the most significant risks to the tea industry. Erratic rainfall, prolonged dry spells, excessive heat stress, floods and pest infestations adversely impacted crop productivity, leaf quality and overall production during the year, and may affect both availability and pricing of quality teas. Development work in all gardens was impacted by adverse weather during FY 25-26.
- MD&A cites market volatility from fluctuations in auction prices, changing consumer demand patterns and uneven market demand, which may continue to affect price realizations and operating margins. The Company's own average sale price for own-leaf tea declined to Rs.390.68 per kg and bought-leaf realisation fell by Rs 30.21 per kg to Rs 159.63 per kg due to a subdued market.
- The Assam tea sector faces labour shortages, increasing wage-related costs and labour absenteeism, which exert pressure on production economics and estate productivity. Management states profitability came under pressure due to a sharp increase in wages, and that cost of production rose mainly on account of wage revision.
- The Board's report and MD&A both flag that bank borrowings increased with a consequential increase in interest cost, driven by higher cost of production and lower sale volumes; profitability was hurt by increased borrowing arising from a shortage of working capital finance and repayment of term loan.
- MD&A future-outlook section flags rising input costs — increasing wages, higher energy expenses and inflationary pressure on fertilizers and other agricultural inputs — as continuing to impact the cost structure of tea producers, alongside pressure on operating margins.
- MD&A 'Supply Chain Disruptions' cites geopolitical developments, international trade restrictions, evolving food safety regulations, residue compliance requirements, shipping delays, container shortages and freight cost fluctuations as risks that may impact export competitiveness and timely deliveries.
- The business is concentrated in tea manufacture from estates located in Assam, so the climatic, labour and auction-price factors described in the MD&A act on essentially the entire revenue base; there is no diversification narrative in the report beyond retail expansion within tea.
- MD&A 'Threats and Challenges' notes intensifying competition from coffee, energy drinks and health-based alternatives, particularly among younger demographics, requiring innovation and strategic repositioning by tea brands.
